citeAs: Pratap, V., Xu, Q., Sriram, A., Synnaeve, G., Collobert, R. (2020). MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish). It also includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
inLanguage: en, de, nl, fr, es, it, pt, pl
name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human transcribers verified development and test set transcripts; no demographic details about the transcribers are provided. The gender classifier was validated on Dutch and Polish speakers with 96% and 94% accuracy respectively.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript (GT) and human rated transcript (HRT) was measured for dev and test sets across all 8 languages. English dev/test: 4.55/4.54; German: 3.6/3.9; Dutch: 7.24/8.61; French: 3.33/4.45; Spanish: 1.93/3.07; Italian: 6.8/5.37; Portuguese: 12.64/12.07; Polish: 5.67/5.12.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts for development and test sets were human-verified: human transcribers listened to audio while reading the generated transcript and corrected clear and obvious errors. For training data, transcripts were generated automatically via pseudo-label generation and transcript retrieval (TF-IDF + Smith-Waterman alignment). Gender labels were assigned using an SVM gender classifier trained on LibriSpeech speakers.
rai:dataBiases: To avoid introducing bias from human transcription, transcribers were instructed to only correct "clear and obvious" errors. The MLS English development and test sets were deliberately chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions (speakers with WER higher than 80% of those in dev-other sets were selected). Gender balance was enforced in development and test sets. The dataset is derived from public domain audiobooks, which may over-represent certain genres, time periods, or demographics of authors and readers.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks downloaded from LibriVox, covering 8 languages (English, German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish). LibriVox audiobooks were downloaded using data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. Audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models. Pseudo labels were generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model. Transcripts were retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to available book text sources using TF-IDF similarity and Smith-Waterman alignment.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox, with text sources from Project Gutenberg, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, and other online sources. LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data are released in the public domain.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read speech (audiobooks), which may not generalize to conversational or spontaneous speech. For Polish, the high OOV rate (13.39%) negatively impacts language model decoding performance. Some audiobook text sources were unavailable or had invalid links, requiring manual search for alternatives. The dataset may not cover all speakers or dialects equally due to the nature of LibriVox volunteer recordings.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dataset was split into train, development, and test sets with no speaker overlap across splits. Speakers were balanced by gender and duration in development and test sets. Speakers with duration shorter than a threshold were assigned to training set; speakers with high duration were truncated by sampling recordings up to an upper bound. Limited supervision subsets were created: 10-hour, 1-hour, and six 10-minute sets per language, with balanced male/female speaker sampling.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments based on silence intervals. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering of characters outside the language's valid unicode range. Numbers in text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied to handle hyphens and apostrophes. Candidate transcripts with WER > 40% between candidate transcript and pseudo label were filtered out. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or duplicate versions were removed.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to open new avenues in ASR and TTS research by providing a large, freely available multilingual speech corpus. It promotes open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, addressing the scarcity of open-licensed, large-scale speech datasets for non-English languages.
rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research, including large-scale multilingual ASR training and benchmarking; Text-to-Speech (TTS) research as an extension of LibriTTS to a larger multilingual setting; low-resource ASR research using the limited supervision subsets.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss for audio segmentation and pseudo-label generation; wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference; 4-gram language models for beam-search decoding; TF-IDF similarity scoring on bigrams for document retrieval; Smith-Waterman alignment for transcript matching; SVM gender classifier with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech speakers for gender labeling; pdftotext tool for extracting text from PDF/EPUB books.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; human verification was done once per item for dev/test sets.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper mentions some audiobook text sources had invalid links or were unavailable, and manual searches were conducted to find alternatives, but does not describe a formal missing data handling protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol for missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is derived from public domain audiobooks; no personal or sensitive information is collected. The paper notes that in-house training data used for acoustic models was completely de-identified.
